newsitem.title: USA: Union Pacific increases capital spending.
newsitem.headline: Union Pacific increases capital spending.

text.p: Union Pacific Resources Group Inc said in a statement with second quarter earnings that it would increase its 1997 capital spending budget to $1.5 billion from $1.0 billion as a result of a series of property acquisitions.
During the second quarter UPR bought assets in East Texas and agreed to buy Highlands Gas Co.
Jack Messman, UPR's chairman and chief executive, said that the company was operating 61 rigs, an increase of 17 rigs from the third quarter of 1996.
It also launched a hostile bid for Pennzoil Co.
Net income for the huge independent oil and gas company rose in the second quarter to $0.30 per share from $0.28 a year ago.
Discretionary cash flow rose 16 percent year-on-year to quarter discretionary cash flow of $276.2 million ($1.10 per share) and net income six percent to $74.4 million on revenues of $444.6 million.
Year to date discretionary cashflow is up 30 percent at $597.3 million and net income is up 48 percent to $191.6 million.
Analysts had been looking for second quarter earnings per share of $0.30 from UPR.

Total production in the second quarter averaged 1,627.8 million cubic feet of natural gas equivalent, up 11 percent from a year ago and natural gas prices rose in the quarter to $1.85 per thousand cubic feet from $1.68 a year ago.
"Our annual objective is 10 percent earnings growth in a year and we are well on our way to beating that," said president George Lindahl.
The main increases in production came from the Austin Chalk, where volumes rose six percent and the Neumann 2 well in Washington County, Texas was recently completed and is producing 36.8 MMcfd.
It is a direct offset to UPR's Neumann 1 which has now produced over 15 billion cubic feet of gas in 11 months.
The West Texas region also showed strong growth as the result of horizontal drilling programs. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
